prompt:
Draw a NEW ORIGINAL game sprite sheet of a heavy ash-furred brown grizzly BEAR WALKING. Extremely detailed crisp pixel clusters, charcoal-black singed fur tips, grey ash shoulder hump, warm dark brown face, small round ears, short broad muzzle, tiny stub tail, realistic massive 340kg four-legged bear anatomy. Muted natural game lighting, no outline stickers, not a dog or cartoon. Camera elevated three-quarter top-down. Not existing copyrighted game sprites.

The anatomy of the WALK is the main task. Four equal ROWS are directions, exactly FOUR bears per row: FRONT in row1 (face to bottom); LEFT row2 (nose left); RIGHT row3 (nose right); BACK row4 (face away to top, rump visible). Four COLUMNS are walking phases A B C D. 16 whole sprites on transparent RGBA only, generous empty gutters, no floor or shadows or grid or labels. Same bear size across all cells, every silhouette well inside its cell.

WALK PHASE A column1: LEFT forepaw contacts ahead while RIGHT forepaw is behind. WALK PHASE B column2: LEFT forepaw moves back UNDER chest and RIGHT forepaw visibly lifts up in a bent leg. WALK PHASE C column3: RIGHT forepaw contacts ahead while LEFT forepaw is behind. WALK PHASE D column4: RIGHT forepaw moves back UNDER chest and LEFT forepaw visibly lifts up in a bent leg. Alternate hind feet naturally with four-legged support. Make front/rear feet change visibly, slow heavy walk, not running, not upright.

VERY SPECIFIC FRONT row1: in column1 the VIEWER-LEFT front paw is ahead and lower; in column2 that paw is under chest and VIEWER-RIGHT forepaw lifts; in column3 the VIEWER-RIGHT front paw is ahead and lower with VIEWER-LEFT paw tucked higher/back; in column4 viewer-left forepaw visibly lifts off ground. Columns1 and3 MUST have opposite paw ahead. The BACK row similarly alternates viewer-left/viewer-right rear paws, showing a lifted paw sole at the two passing frames.

LEFT and RIGHT SIDE rows: Column1 the nearest visible foreleg stretches ahead, column2 nearest foreleg is upright under shoulder while far forepaw lifts, column3 the nearest visible foreleg stretches BACK and far foreleg stretches AHEAD (both forelegs readable), column4 nearest forepaw lifts bent upward with far forepaw supporting under shoulder. Do NOT stretch the same nearest foreleg ahead in every column. Draw distinct leg positions rather than only a shifted texture. Four REAL DIFFERENT gait keyposes per direction, no duplicated standing poses. Maintain at least two/three grounded support paws, no extra limbs, no disconnected paws or overlap, no weapons, gear, magic, blood, text or scenery.
